subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool-execution dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in tools, plugin tools, client tools, hooks, deferred catalog tools, and agent-core execution?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose this because the feature is a user-trusted security boundary, and the proposed process-global CLI-only shape may miss concurrent or non-CLI execution paths.

options.title: Design request-scoped dry-run
options.body: Specify request-scoped runtime semantics first, then implement the additive core mode with coverage across built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, deferred-tool, and agent-core paths.

options.title: Fold into safe workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent work chooses shared mode vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep command-specific dry-runs plus sandbox/tool-policy controls if maintainers decide global preview would be too easy to mistake for a sandbox.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify request-scoped runtime semantics first, then implement the additive core mode with coverage across built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, deferred-tool, and agent-core paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal for the shared agent runtime and tool adapter boundary where this contract would likely be defined.
